What happened?
Good morning. You look tired. What happened?
A long day. We landed at six forty, and my bag was not on the belt.
Oh no. Was it missing?
Yes. I waited for forty minutes, and then I asked at the counter.
Were they helpful?
Yes, they were. I filled in a form with my hotel and my phone number.
And the bag? Is it here now?
It is. It stayed in Lisbon, but they delivered it at seven thirty last night. Finally.
That happened to me in March. My bag stayed in Chicago for three days.
Three days? That is terrible. What happened?
I shopped for new clothes, and the airline paid for them. And honestly? I liked the new clothes.
So it was a lucky problem.
Exactly. A lucky problem.

Last Tuesday was the worst travel day of my year. I arrived at the airport early, at five in the morning. The flight was at seven, but at six it changed to nine. I waited. Then it changed to eleven. I waited again. At eleven they canceled it. So I walked to the counter, I asked for a new flight, and I booked a seat on the evening flight. I called my wife, I called the hotel, and I called the office, in that order. The evening flight landed at midnight, and I checked in at the hotel at one in the morning. The room was comfortable, and I was too tired to care. And you know what? My bag arrived with me, on the same flight. That was the good part.

My first day in Tokyo was very simple, and it is my favorite day of that trip. I landed at six in the morning, and I was very tired, so I walked slowly from the hotel to the river. I stopped at a small coffee shop, and the owner talked to me for twenty minutes, with his hands and three words of English. In the afternoon I visited a market, and I tasted eleven things. Eleven. I liked ten of them. In the evening it rained, so I stayed in the hotel. I ordered dinner in the room and I watched the rain on the window. It was a quiet day, and I loved it. Today I do not remember the museums from that trip. I remember the coffee shop.
